findings.title: Close the relationships between content type, JSON status, and retention mode
findings.evidence: Static control-flow proof: start from a valid NON_STRING snapshot for content=123 or null (chars/bytes/sha256=None, json ancillary fields=None, evidence={mode:UNAVAILABLE,fragments:[],omitted_chars:None}). Changing json.status to UNAVAILABLE passes lines 450-453 because only NON_STRING implies non-string, with no converse. Independently changing evidence.mode to OMITTED_POLICY or OMITTED_BUDGET passes lines 481-505: omitted_chars None equals expected None and the final branch only requires empty fragments. For an unencodable string (bytes=None), the same mode change also passes although no full-content scan or byte-budget retention could have occurred. No product function was executed during review.
findings.impact: The data-only v5 decoder/exporter accepts contradictory evidence about whether content existed as text and why it was withheld. This can mislead output-structure diagnosis, the purpose of this change. It does not grant delivery credit or bypass native length/write/ACK gates.
findings.requested_fix: Enforce NON_STRING iff content.type is not string; non-string content must have evidence UNAVAILABLE. Require evidence UNAVAILABLE iff content is non-string or UTF-8 bytes are unavailable, matching the current builder. Require OMITTED_POLICY and OMITTED_BUDGET to refer to an encodable string with measured length/hash and empty fragments. Preserve JSON UNAVAILABLE for genuine parsing/measurement failure of string content; do not prohibit a parse-failed but encodable string from having safely retained text. Add targeted negative cases for non-string status mutation, non-string omitted modes, unencodable-string omitted modes, and encodable-text UNAVAILABLE retention mutation; retain positive parser-unavailable cases.
findings.verification: Read-only source/AST reasoning; existing 969 recorded checks do not cover these mutations.
